name: SBI Life Insurance Company Ltd
title: SBI Life Insurance Company Ltd - 540719 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q1 FY27 VoNB up 29% to INR14.1bn but margin fell to 26.2% on a one-off GTI group contract (about 60bps drag per management); IRP growth 14% and management reiterated 26–28% margin guidance.

summary.headline: SBI Life Q1 FY27 VNB rose 29% to INR14.1bn, but VNB margin fell to 26.2% as GST and a one-off GTI group deal diluted mix.
summary.overview: Individual rated premium grew 14% to INR39.7bn with private market share of 22.2%, and all product segments and channels grew. Profit after tax rose 22% to INR7.2bn, helped by supportive market conditions, while the GST impact was INR2.3bn for the quarter. VNB margin of 26.2% was down year on year, which management attributed mainly to a higher share of lumpy group business (GTI) in APE. Management said the margin was within its 26–28% guidance, at the lower end, and expects it to move to the upper end as individual mix normalises.

financial_highlights.change: Margin down YoY; GST impact INR2.3bn

segments.name: Individual rated premium / APE
segments.commentary: Individual APE INR39.9bn, +14% YoY; ULIP INR24.5bn (61% share vs 65% in Q1 FY26); guaranteed non-par savings INR9.7bn, +27%. Non-ULIP share of IRP reached 38%.

segments.name: Group business
segments.commentary: Group NBP INR32.9bn (37% of NBP), +41% YoY; group APE INR53.8bn, +36%; group protection APE INR12.3bn, +313%, driven by a large one-off GTI contract.

segments.name: Protection
segments.commentary: Individual protection APE INR1.9bn, +18%; pure protection +41% on individual APE; ROP share of individual protection 68% vs 73% a year ago.

segments.name: Bancassurance (SBI and RRBs)
segments.commentary: 47% of total APE; individual APE INR24.5bn, +10%; SBI branch productivity INR4.1mn, +7%. Other banks grew 19% on individual NBP and 31% on APE; their mix is about 80% non-ULIP.

segments.name: Agency
segments.commentary: Individual APE INR13.1bn, +20%; agent productivity INR2 lakh; non-ULIP share rose from 43% to 46%; 34,000+ agents added gross and 11 new branches opened.

segments.name: Other channels (direct, corporate agents, brokers, online)
segments.commentary: Grew 160% and contributed 28% of total APE; management did not split this into organic and group components.

guidance_outlook: IRP growth guidance of 14–15% for FY27 reaffirmed.
VNB margin guidance of 26–28% for FY27 maintained; management expects the margin to move toward the upper end as individual mix normalises.
GST drag expected for one more quarter (Q2 FY27), with the impact ending thereafter; GST was waived from 22 September, so about 2.5 months of impact remain in Q1.
Pure protection growth expected to keep outpacing ROP; the company is shifting focus from ROP to non-ROP and pure protection.
Regular-pay deferred annuity plan expected to launch within the next quarter.
Non-ULIP share of IRP targeted to be sustained at around this level for the year.
Other-expense ratio expected to normalise over the next three quarters, but higher stamp duty tied to sum assured growth will persist.
capex_capacity: Agency network: more than 100 branches opened over the last two to three years, and 11 new branches in Q1 FY27.
Agent additions: over 34,000 agents added on a gross basis in Q1 FY27.
New corporate agency tie-up with J&K Bank; business expected to start in the current quarter.
Automation: 99.9% of individual proposals submitted digitally; 67% processed through automated underwriting.
demand_pricing: Individual sum assured grew 46% YoY and group new business sum assured grew 265%; rider sum assured is 39% of individual sum assured.
Rider attachment on ULIP is about 45–50%, up from roughly 35% when introduced about 1–1.5 years ago; management expects it to hold or improve.
Non-par pricing is reviewed against yield movements; IRR for customers was raised in June after the yield curve moved.
The 61st-month persistency dip is attributed to the COVID cohort moving through policy years; management expects it to normalise by end-Q3 FY27.
Credit protect business was flat YoY; management expects an uptick in coming quarters.
Misselling ratio 0.02%; death claim settlement ratio 98.8%.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 60 bps product-mix drag on VNB margin is due to the GTI group deal, and what is the normalised margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 60 bps mix drag relates only to GTI and that the company does not disclose product-wise margins. It said margin should return to normal as IRP share normalises. The 40 bps assumption-related item reflects the March 2026 annual review, and there was no assumption change in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Is the GST drag going to persist, and how do expenses look?
qa_highlights.answer: GST drag of about 1.1 percentage points in Q1 is expected to continue into Q2 and then fade. Management said the rise in other expenses reflects one-off stamp duty tied to higher sum assured and labour code impacts, and it expects these to normalise over the next three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will agency growth be sustainable and will the channel mix shift affect costs or margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Agency APE grew 20% in Q1, with the current quarter at 19%-plus. Management expects a stronger contribution from agency in the remaining three quarters and a balanced mix of banca and agency going forward. It did not discuss cost impact in detail.

qa_highlights.question: What proportion of ULIPs carry rider attachment, and how is protection classified?
qa_highlights.answer: Rider attachment on ULIPs is about 45–50%, up from roughly 35% when riders were introduced 1–1.5 years earlier. Riders are counted within individual protection, and rider APE was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Why is individual protection growth lower than peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the shift from ROP to pure protection lowers ticket size, which makes headline growth look subdued. Individual protection grew 22% by its own measure against pure protection growth of 41%, with ROP share at 68%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the regular-pay deferred annuity plan launch slip, and what are the non-par and regulatory views?
qa_highlights.answer: The deferred annuity plan is expected in the next quarter and is being developed for an opportune time. On non-par, management said pricing is reviewed against yield movements. On regulation, management said it sees the company as well placed and expects future rules to be positive for the industry.

risks_watch: Group/GTI lumpiness: a large one-off group contract diluted Q1 VNB margin; sustainability of group APE mix and margin recovery to 26–28% range is the key test.
GST drag of about 110 bps on margin in Q1 FY27 with another quarter expected; watch whether Q2 drag falls as indicated.
Other-expense ratio rising (opex ratio 7.7% vs 6.3%) due to stamp duty and labour codes; watch cost discipline.
61st-month persistency dip due to COVID cohort; management expects normalisation by end-Q3 FY27.
Credit protect flat YoY; watch for the promised uptick.
Rider APE not disclosed; pure protection ticket size is smaller, so protection growth optics may stay weaker than peers.
Regulatory changes flagged as an open question by management; details not yet clear.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line growth and the full-year IRP and VNB margin guidance, but defensive on the margin decline, which it attributed to one-off group business and GST. Management was evasive on quantifying the GTI margin drag and product-level margins, and declined to comment on individual contracts.
key_quotes: The margin guidance was 26% to 28%, and we are within the range, although at the lower end of that.
And going forward, with higher focus on individual policies, the margin is going to be towards the upper range of our guidance.
So the GST was waived from 22nd of September. So there will be some impact for 2.5 months in the current quarter also.
Hopefully within next quarter, you will be able to see that.

adds.what: 11 new agency branches opened in Q1 FY27 (more than 100 over last 2-3 years)
New corporate agency tie-up with J&K Bank
Regular-pay deferred annuity plan launch (product, not capacity)

growth.why: Management reaffirmed FY27 individual rated premium growth of 14-15% and VNB margin of 26-28% (toward upper end), backed by agency branch and agent additions, a J&K Bank tie-up, a planned annuity launch and a shift toward pure protection; no quantified capacity or order book, so backing is partial.
